newsitem.title: INDIA: Foreign funds propel India shares to 33-mth high.
newsitem.headline: Foreign funds propel India shares to 33-mth high.

text.p: ** (1300 GMT) India shares break through psychological
** Foreign funds pour money into blue-chip stocks, broaden
** Benchmark Bombay index leaps 2.28 pct to 4,404.69
** Delhi index rises 20.35 pts, or 2.24 pct, to 935.17,
CRISIL-500 18.77 pts, or 2.4 pct, to 797.16, Madras index 49 pts, or 1.15 pct, to 4,323.65
Heavy foreign fund buying drove Indian shares sharply higher on Wednesday with the benchmark Bombay index breaking through a psychological barrier to reach new 33-month peaks, brokers said.
"There's been frenzied buying by FIIs (foreign institutional investors)," said Sanat Dalal, a top broker at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). "They are accumulating all the blue-chips."
The 30-share BSE index finished 99.30 points, or 2.28 percent, higher at 4,404.69 -- breaking through 4,400 for the first time since mid-October 1994.
"It has crossed the barrier. The market looks in very good shape," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs.
Traders said the buoyant market was drawing in more investors while sellers were becoming more choosy.
"The biggest point to note is that the most prominent seller has stopped selling," said Dalal, referring to the Unit Trust of India (UTI), the country's largest mutual fund.
The UTI was currently collecting funds through sale of units at the start of its financial year which began on July 1, a UTI official said, adding that he expected the index to go up.
UTI expects to raise 120-150 billion rupees in fiscal 1997/98, its chairman said recently.
Other dealers said foreign funds were enlarging their portfolios by buying into new sectors.
"The FIIs are strengthening their portfolios by adding multinational shares to other blue-chips," said Arun Shah, chief dealer at brokerage P.R. Subramanyan & Sons.
